Omar (procurement): FYI attached the vendor X commercial. Can someone confirm how their SKUs map to our usage buckets? I'm worried the commit tiers aren't aligned with our token mix.
Lucy (solutions-eng): looks like they split by 'generation tokens' vs 'context tokens' and have separate embedding lines. I'll paste the excerpt below.
Lucy (solutions-eng): ```
- Commit A: 5M generation tokens / mo = $3,000/mo
- Commit B: 20M generation tokens / mo = $10,500/mo
- Overage generation: $0.0006 / token
- Context (input) tokens billed at $0.0002 / token
- Embeddings: $0.018 / 1k vectors
```
Nate (eng): hmm our 95th percentile workload is more context-heavy (long prompts + retrieval). That Commit A looks undersized for context. Do they allow splitting generation vs context commits?
Omar (procurement): vendor said 'commits are pooled per account' but the fine print mentions separate metering. Asking for clarification.
Jess (finance): also confirm how they report usage — does the invoice break out generation vs input tokens? We need that for our internal chargebacks and for GAAP deferral.
Lucy (solutions-eng): vendor sales chat said invoices show line items but not at prompt-level. We can request custom metering export for enterprise deals.
Omar (procurement): asked for two things: 1) a mapping doc that ties their SKUs to our internal SKUs (generation/context/embeddings); 2) price table if we split commits by SKU vs pooled commit. Waiting on their redlines.
Nate (eng): can someone run a quick expected cost calc for our current prod usage if we move to their pricing? I'll post numbers.
Lucy (solutions-eng): rough calc: current monthly: 3M gen tokens, 25M context tokens, 2M embed vectors. With Commit B blended + overage it's ~ $10.5k commit covers gen but context adds ~ $5k => ~ $15.5k/mo. (very rough)
Jess (finance): that looks ~2x our current hosted spend. Need to validate with proper attribution. Also check if they offer committed discounts for embeddings (we use a lot).
Omar (procurement): vendor offered a one-year term with a 10% discount on commit if we sign in the quarter. Also listed an onboarding credit of $5k. Thoughts?
Nate (eng): onboarding credit is nice. But commit mismatch is the risk — we could either: 1) bucket context-heavy workloads to a cheaper model variant, or 2) negotiate a split commit where context tokens have a lower rate.
Lucy (solutions-eng): propose a counter: split commit 60% context / 40% generation and lower context rate to $0.00015/token, plus embeddings at $0.015/1k for first year. Should buy down our cost.
Jess (finance): also ask about billing cadence and true-up process. We need monthly true-ups and a PO-friendly invoice. If they require prepaid annual commit it impacts cash.
Omar (procurement): @Jess noted. I'm drafting an email to vendor with ask list: SKU mapping, sample invoice, EOM true-up terms, ability to export per-token CSV, and counter on split commit + embedding discount. Will share draft.
vendor-checker-bot: Vendor X is not on the preferred-vendor list. Flagging: security intake incomplete. Please run security questionnaire before contracting. :warning:
Omar (procurement): thanks bot — added Security intake to the checklist. Ping @Lucy's team to start the questionnaire (they'll need to provide model eval artefacts).
Lucy (solutions-eng): will take point on the security packet. Can someone from infra share contact for secure environment tests?
Nate (eng): tagging infra offline. Also recommend adding a usage cap + automated fallback policy in the contract to avoid runaway overage charges.
Jess (finance): +1 on caps. Also request invoice level columns: commit used, overage quantity, unit prices, and a CSV export for chargeback.
Omar (procurement): OK I'll send the ask list and the counter-proposal today. If vendor responds with sample invoice and CSV export, we can fast-track legal review.
Lucy (solutions-eng): sounds good. leaning toward trial with a 30-day pilot first (no minimum) to validate cost model. Any objections?
Jess (finance): no objections, but require invoice-level visibility during pilot.
Nate (eng): fine with pilot. We'll route traffic to their staging endpoints only.
Omar (procurement): great — I'll update the thread when vendor replies. :rocket:
